analysis: Examined head-side lines 1380-2230 of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift (two units). The visible change is two new default-inert members on ClusterOnboardingOperations: stopsAsked (default nil) at line 1521 and serveUnlessStopped (default nil) at line 1525. Neither is in init, and only the live operations set them. Defaults preserve the previous behavior. These are local CLI onboarding closures; they add no network, crypto, attestation, or authorization surface in the visible text. The doc comments say serveUnlessStopped is checked on the leading Mac under the start lock so a stop that took the lock first is never undone. That is a local stop-versus-start race control, relevant to availability (A-018 and T-059/T-060 style local control). The enforcement is outside the supplied units, so this pass cannot verify it. The other visible hunk, outside these units, changes the provision call to pass stopsBefore: nil at about line 2852, which is the pre-adopt refusal path with no serve. The rest of the supplied text (pairing state machine, console protocol, allowLocalNetwork) is unchanged context. It carries code confirmation on each Mac, with no 'yes' relayed across the cable, and Local Network handling. None of that is modified. Remaining integration questions: (1) where the live stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped are implemented (likely the leader's ClusterSetupRecord under its start lock) and whether the stop counter can be read or forged by an unauthenticated peer over the control channel; (2) whether a nil stopsBefore, the old-build fallback, skips the stop check as intended; (3) the later hunks of the file (provision with stopsBefore, around lines 2901-3535), which are not in these units. I identified no concrete regression from the supplied evidence.
